nodes.name: Every 5 min
nodes.notes: ADR-056 Block 5: depth/health dead-man's-switch for the BullMQ application queue. Every 5 min it GETs the queue-consumer's /metrics, which returns BullMQ job counts PLUS a consumer-COMPUTED alert (the consumer owns all queue.* thresholds — ADR-056 R4 — so this cron stays thresholds-free and just forwards a present alert). Catches: a wedged worker (jobs waiting, none draining), an absolute flood, and a rising failed/DLQ set. The consumer-DOWN case is owned by the faster host heartbeat dead-man's-switch (consumer-heartbeat.timer, ~120s); this cron's HTTP-unreachable branch is a secondary WARN.

nodes.name: When Called
nodes.notes: Test entry for Definition-of-Done verification via scripts/test-subworkflow.mjs (a Schedule Trigger cannot be fired over the n8n API). No inputs needed.

nodes.name: Get Queue Metrics
nodes.notes: GET http://queue-consumer:8080/metrics over the internal docker network (no public round-trip). Returns { ok, counts:{waiting,active,completed,failed,delayed,paused}, thresholds, alert:{severity,message,details}|null }. 2xx with alert=null = healthy. Any non-2xx / network error routes to the error output (onError) -> WARN (monitoring itself degraded; the heartbeat owns the consumer-down CRITICAL).

nodes.name: Alert Present?
nodes.notes: The consumer already decided whether to alarm (it owns the thresholds). True -> forward its alert to Post Alert; false -> silent NoOp (a healthy poll must NOT post to the Alerts task every 5 min). main[1] is the false branch.

nodes.name: Post Depth Alert
nodes.notes: Forwards the consumer-computed alert (WARN or CRITICAL) into Post Alert (v1) seam (ADR-025). Severity/message/details come straight from /metrics — the consumer decided them. Source queue-consumer/depth.

nodes.name: Healthy
nodes.notes: Terminal for the healthy path. Silent on purpose — a healthy queue must NOT post every 5 min.

nodes.name: Alert Metrics Unreachable
nodes.notes: The /metrics GET failed (non-2xx or network). WARN, not CRITICAL: the host heartbeat dead-man's-switch (consumer-heartbeat.timer) owns the consumer-DOWN CRITICAL within ~120s; this is the slower, secondary 'the depth monitor itself can't see the queue' signal. If both fire, the heartbeat is the authoritative one.
